[[ ## thread ## ]]
From: Marco Petrosyan
To: Gabriel Fontes, Sylvia Nakamura
Subject: Tip reporting for this quarter — numbers look off

Hey Gabriel and Sylvia,

Quick one — I was looking at the tip numbers for the quarter and something doesn’t sit right. We’re seeing a dip that doesn’t match what I’m hearing from the floor, and I want to make sure we’re not missing something before we file. Could you both take a look and flag any discrepancies? If it’s a timing thing or a coding issue, fine, but I need to know by end of week so we can adjust.

Thanks,
Marco

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Marco Petrosyan
Subject: RE: Tip reporting for this quarter — numbers look off

Hi Marco,

Thanks for flagging this. I took a close look at the tip numbers against the payroll and sales data for the quarter, and I don't see a coding or data-entry issue on our side. The dip appears to be a timing matter rather than a reporting error.

What's happening: a portion of tips earned in the last few days of the quarter landed in the next payroll cycle, so they didn't hit this quarter's numbers. That's a normal cut-off lag, and it should self-correct in the next period. I've also double-checked the tip allocation by outlet and by shift, and nothing else stands out as off.

I can walk you through the detail if helpful — happy to set aside 15 minutes before Thursday. Just let me know what works.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Marco Petrosyan
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: RE: Tip reporting for this quarter — numbers look off

Gabriel,

Thanks for digging in — that timing explanation makes sense, and I appreciate you checking the allocation by outlet and shift. Let's do the 15 minutes before Thursday; I'd rather see the detail than guess. Send me a time that works.

Also, Sylvia — if you've got anything from your end on this, loop me in when you get a chance. Want to make sure we're all on the same page before we file.

Talk soon,
Marco

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Marco Petrosyan
Subject: RE: Tip reporting for this quarter — numbers look off

Hi Marco,

Great — let's get it on the calendar. I have time Thursday morning; how does 9:30 AM work for you? I'll send a calendar invite shortly.

For the walkthrough, I'll walk through the quarter-end cut-off on tips, show the payroll cycle dates, and point to where the lagging amount lands in the current period. I'll also bring the allocation-by-outlet and by-shift detail so you can see there's nothing else flagged.

One note for context: the dip is roughly $46k and ties to September's last payroll cycle, so you should see that amount flow into Q4 numbers as expected. Supporting documentation is already in the shared drive under the quarterly close folder if you want to peek ahead.

Let me know if Thursday morning doesn't work and we'll find another slot before the end of the week.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Marco Petrosyan
Subject: RE: Tip reporting for this quarter — numbers look off

Hi Marco,

Great — I'll get something on your calendar for tomorrow. As a heads-up, I've already pulled the detail by outlet and shift, plus the payroll cut-off dates, so we can walk through exactly where the lag lands and confirm it flows into next quarter.

Quick note on Sylvia: I haven't seen anything from her end on this, but I'll make sure to loop her in if she has input before our call. If you'd like, I can also send over a one-page summary after we meet so you have it for your files.

Let me know if tomorrow morning works, or if another time is better.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

---

From: Sylvia Nakamura
To: Marco Petrosyan
Subject: RE: Tip reporting for this quarter — numbers look off

Hi Marco,

Thanks for looping me in. I've reviewed the tip reporting from my side as well, and I'm aligned with Gabriel's read — the dip is a timing lag on tips earned in the last few days of the quarter that fell into the next payroll cycle. I don't see any data-entry or coding issues in the payroll records I handle.

One note for completeness: the quarterly filing itself is still on track for the deadline. If you'd like, I can pull the payroll cycle cut-off dates for the quarter and confirm the exact dates in writing before you finalize.

Happy to join the call with Gabriel if that's helpful, or I can just send over the cut-off dates by end of day Thursday.

Best,
Sylvia

---

From: Sylvia Nakamura
To: Marco Petrosyan
Subject: RE: Tip reporting for this quarter — numbers look off

Hi Marco,

Thanks for the note. I've gone through the tip figures from the payroll side and confirm Gabriel's read — the dip is a timing lag. Tips earned in the last few days of September landed in the first payroll cycle of October, so they didn't make this quarter's numbers. There's no data-entry or coding issue in the records I handle.

To have it in writing before you finalize, I can pull the exact payroll cycle cut-off dates for the quarter and confirm them in an email by end of day Thursday. If it's easier, I can also join the call with Gabriel and walk through those dates alongside his detail.

Let me know which you'd prefer. The quarterly filing itself is still on track for the deadline.

Best,
Sylvia
